newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's mutual funds raise $264.3 mln in 9 mths.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's mutual funds raise $264.3 mln in 9 mths.

text.p: Morocco's mutual funds, new operators on the bourse, raised a total of 2.3 billion dirhams ($264.3 million) in the first nine months of the year, a market analyst said on Friday.

The mutual funds "registered a sustained development in recent months...They raised 2.3 billion dirhams in the first nine months of the year, but they remain unkown to the general public," Ali Amar, a market analyst wrote in the authoritative Casablanca-based weekly La Vie Economique.

A group of 14 mutual funds were allowed for the first time by the stock market watchdog Conseil Deontologique Des Valeurs Mobilieres (CDVM) to operate on the bourse in January 1996. The officials use the term, OPCVM, (Organismes de Placement Collectifs en Valeurs Mobilieres) to describe mutual funds.
Hassan Bouhemou, president of the Moroccan Association of Investment Trusts and Funds said the first target was institutional investors and the next would be small investors.
"The funds raised an average of 45 million dirhams per week this year...With a more aggressive marketing policy, the funds could easily double their assets next year," he added.
